description: openLCA's LCIA package writes its registry numbers zero-padded to six digits -- `000108-90-7` on 51,173 of its 55,630 numbers -- and a lookup query carrying such a number found nothing, because the index holds `108-90-7` (#375). Every list's adapter already read its numbers through one normaliser, now `domain.registry_numbers.normalize_cas_number`, and the EF 3.1 adapter joins them; a query's number goes through the same function as its first preparation step, for every caller, and the answer says `registry-number-padding`. That half is the lookup's and is held by tests/test_lookup_matcher.py. What a build can be asked is that the package's padded numbers reach the substances they name: the issue's own example rows, placed by their number.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Pronamide` rows, written with 023950-58-5, reach propyzamide by the number 23950-58-5
expectations.comment: The package writes `023950-58-5`; the adapter reads `23950-58-5` and the rows reach the one substance carrying it. Held so the adapter never stops unpadding.

expectations.title: openLCA's `Benzene, chloro-` rows, written with 000108-90-7, reach chlorobenzene by the number 108-90-7
expectations.comment: Sixteen flows and 1,628 factors on the issue's measure, the largest unplaced name when the padding was not read.
